questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.**

In ones and twos
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**In small numbers**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• "**In ones and twos**" is an idiom that means "**in small numbers**".
 
• When something is happening "in ones and twos," it implies that it is occurring in a limited or small quantity, rather than in large groups or numbers.
 
• This phrase is often used to describe situations where only a few people or things are involved, and it emphasizes the scarcity or limited nature of the occurrence.
 
• It is also used to describe people or things arriving or leaving slowly or gradually.
 
 
• **Example**: *The guests arrived at the party in ones and twos throughout the evening.*
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.
